issues: “King Mosiah” is an accurate paraphrase of “king Mosiah,” though the source does not style him as “king” in a standalone character label; he is mentioned background, not present. The summary preserves this distinction.

Pride is described figuratively as being “lifted up”; the scene correctly prohibits literal levitation. The three developments are a summary, not established as simultaneous.

The unspecified location is acceptable, but the scene does not establish where the encounter occurs.

The source chapter identifies him in Alma 1:15. Preserve the name only as an established identity, not as text explicitly naming him in this scene.

The visual inference of Nehor and the people carrying him on the hilltop is consistent with the verse. “There” locates his acknowledgment and death on the hill; the wording “between the heavens and the earth” should remain nonliteral as the notes require.

“Place of labor” is listed as a location, but the source does not specify where the teaching or labor occurred. Keep it generic and avoid presenting it as a particular location.

The scene appropriately treats abundance and generosity as reported conditions, not a single distribution event. The broad visual inference should not imply that all listed goods and recipients appear in one specific encounter.

The source says the law was enforced against transgressors as far as possible; the narration excerpt “the law was put in force upon all those who did transgress it” omits that qualification. It is an exact excerpt, but the summary correctly retains the qualification.
